title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure built on synthetic media. Real, identifiable women had their faces placed onto sexual content they never appeared in, and the material was published on a platform that reportedly encourages anonymous uploads and pays uploaders according to views. The people depicted took no part in the generation and had no opportunity to consent. The harm sits at the platform's upload and payment layer, which is where the material entered circulation and where it earned money.

Catching it would have required a check at that upload or payment step, or a body with the power to order removal. The legal category already existed, since deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn law and is therefore criminal. What the reporting describes as missing is a designated authority to take such images offline, which is what the Beckerman motion proposed. The same reporting records that parliamentary attention faded within a week and that members heard nothing for months afterwards.

What is not established is any finding against the platform itself. The reports describe complaints, a proposed motion and a conditional sentence in an earlier, separate case, not a verdict, and no report establishes intent by anyone involved.

summary:
Multiple Dutch female celebrities are considering legal action after discovering manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos include Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos appalling and urged victims to file complaints. Several victims and their representatives have confirmed they have either filed reports or are considering legal action to address this violation.

Deepfake pornography, where a person's head is digitally placed onto an adult film actor's body, falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. The platform reportedly encourages anonymous uploads and offers payment based on video views. Lawyers advise victims to file reports with police, which may lead authorities to shut down the website. Other options include filing a mass claim, submitting complaints to data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a conditional sentence for creating fake videos of presenter Welmoed Sijtsma.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
